A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SOCO research and contain the complete main paper and 17-page supplementary material. Their text, equations, figures and tables support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v3 reports original vision-model and LVLM evaluations in Tables 2–3, downstream-task correlation analyses in Figure 4, and additional experiments in the appendices.

after.justification: v4 retains these original empirical results, including SOCO evaluations, downstream-task experiments and appendix analyses of evaluation protocols and visual markers.

M1.justification: The SOC framework, feature matching in Equation 1, frozen-backbone probes and LVLM evaluation procedure are unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same SOCO categories and tasks, other correspondence benchmarks in Appendix C.1, and downstream tasks in Section 5.3. Added citations in Table 1 do not expand evaluated coverage.

E2.justification: The evaluated model and comparator sets in the main and appendix experiments are unchanged. DiscoBox already appeared in Table 1; its new citation does not introduce an evaluated baseline.

E3.justification: Both retain the same sampling, metrics, resolutions and probe settings, including 20,000 pairs per CC/SOC/Cross-SOC task and the four-permutation CircularEval protocol for LVLMs.

E4.justification: Appendix A retains the same threshold, viewpoint, category and alternative evaluation-protocol analyses. Appendix D.4 retains the same visual-marker shape and color tests.

E5.justification: Section 5.3 retains 95% bootstrap confidence intervals using 10,000 resamples and leave-one-out checks. Run, seed and uncertainty-reporting practices are unchanged throughout.

E6.justification: Numerical results and qualitative findings match throughout the main paper and appendices. For example, DINOv2 SOC PCK remains 60.4 in Table 2, and Qwen3-VL-8B description-only accuracy remains 54.0 in Table 3.

T1.justification: The definitions of semantic concepts, SOC and cross-category correspondence in Section 3.2, along with the mathematical evaluation formulations, are unchanged. No formal assumptions, derivations or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same benchmark contributions and claims about geometric part awareness, the LVLM text-versus-visual correspondence gap, and SOC's downstream diagnostic value.

C2.justification: Interpretations of repeated-part confusion, cross-category transfer and LVLM behavior are unchanged. Appendix F retains the same limitations concerning sparse annotations, image-source bias, prompting, nearest-neighbor matching and taxonomy scope.

D1.justification: Appendices D–E retain the same model configurations, implementation details, prompts and annotation procedures. The project link and dataset/evaluation-framework release statements are unchanged.

R1.justification: v4 adds the DiscoBox paper by Lan et al. as reference 33 and cites it in the existing Table 1 row. Table 1 also gains citations to already-referenced datasets. The related-work argument and novelty positioning remain unchanged.

P1.justification: Bibliographic edits revise author information, add publication page ranges and expand venue names. Citation numbering and the arXiv version/date change, while the scientific prose and section organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Figure 1 has small visual adjustments while retaining its content. Table 1 widens slightly to accommodate citations, and the bibliography reflows. Experimental figures and tables retain their designs.

improvement.justification: v4 improves attribution and source traceability by adding citations to Table 1, supplying the missing DiscoBox reference and completing bibliography details. The scientific evidence and conclusions are unchanged, so the overall benefit is limited to editorial quality.
